summary_zh: 學會用第二條件句（If I were you… / If the rent were lower…）談租屋的想像與條件，看房、談押金、做入住點交都說得出口。

vocab.definition: a legal agreement to rent a home for a fixed period
vocab.example: We signed a one-year lease on Friday.
vocab.example_zh: 我們星期五簽了一年的租約。

vocab.definition: money you pay a landlord before moving in and get back if nothing is damaged
vocab.example: The landlord asked for a security deposit of two months' rent.
vocab.example_zh: 房東要收兩個月房租當押金。

vocab.definition: basic services such as water, electricity and gas
vocab.example: Does the rent include utilities, or do we pay them separately?
vocab.example_zh: 房租有包水電瓦斯嗎？還是要另外付？

vocab.zh: 讓人直接放棄的關鍵問題
vocab.definition: one problem that is serious enough to make you say no
vocab.example: No natural light is a deal-breaker for me.
vocab.example_zh: 完全沒有自然光，對我來說就是不考慮。

vocab.definition: a home in poor condition that needs a lot of repairs
vocab.example: It's a fixer-upper, so the price is surprisingly low.
vocab.example_zh: 那間需要大整修，所以價格低得驚人。

vocab.zh: （入住或退租時）逐間點交檢查
vocab.definition: a careful check of a home, room by room, usually with the landlord
vocab.example: We did a walk-through and photographed every scratch.
vocab.example_zh: 我們逐間檢查了一遍，把每道刮痕都拍下來。

vocab.definition: close enough to reach on foot
vocab.example: The apartment is within walking distance of a supermarket.
vocab.example_zh: 那間公寓走路就能到超市。

vocab.definition: to rent out all or part of your rented home to someone else
vocab.example: Can I sublet the room while I'm working abroad?
vocab.example_zh: 我在國外工作的期間，可以把房間轉租出去嗎？

reading.title: What I'd Tell Anyone Looking for an Apartment
paragraphs: After six weeks of apartment hunting, my partner Sam and I finally signed a lease last Friday. The place isn't perfect, but it's within walking distance of the train station, and the rent includes utilities, so our monthly costs are easy to predict. If a friend asked me for advice today, here is what I would tell them.

First, go to every viewing with a short list of deal-breakers. For us, mold was one. Sam has asthma that tends to flare up in moldy rooms, and over-the-counter medicine only helps so much. One cheap apartment looked fine in the photos, but the bathroom smelled of mold. If we lived somewhere like that, Sam would probably be sick all winter, so we walked away after five minutes.

Second, don't fall in love with a fixer-upper unless the landlord has agreed in writing to do the repairs. We saw a run-down two-bedroom with beautiful old windows. If I were better at repairs, I would happily take it on myself, but I can barely hang a picture.

Third, negotiate without coming across as difficult. Landlords prefer tenants who are polite and constructive. When one landlord wanted a three-month security deposit, we asked whether he would accept two months if we signed for two years instead of one. He agreed on the spot.

Finally, do a careful walk-through on move-in day and photograph every scratch. If there were a disagreement about damage later, those photos would protect your deposit. It takes twenty minutes, and it could save you hundreds of dollars.

questions.q: Why did the writer and Sam reject the cheap apartment?
options: The photos online were misleading about its size.
The mold in the bathroom could make Sam's asthma worse.
It was too far from the train station.
The landlord wanted a three-month deposit.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：浴室有霉味，而 Sam 的氣喘「tends to flare up in moldy rooms」，住那裡整個冬天都會不舒服。

questions.q: How did they get a smaller security deposit?
options: They paid the first month's rent in advance.
They showed the landlord their bank statements.
They offered to sign a longer lease.
They agreed to pay for the utilities.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：他們問房東，若簽兩年而不是一年，押金能否從三個月降到兩個月，房東當場答應。

questions.q: What can we infer about the run-down two-bedroom?
options: The writer turned it down mainly because of a lack of repair skills.
The landlord refused to fix the old windows.
Sam had a deal-breaker about the windows.
It was more expensive than the apartment they rented.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：作者說「If I were better at repairs, I would happily take it on myself, but I can barely hang a picture」，表示作者其實很喜歡那間，是因為自己不太會修繕才放棄。

grammar.point_zh: 第二條件句：談和現在不符、或不太可能發生的假設

guide.key_zh: 想像「現在其實不是這樣」或「不太可能發生」：If 子句用過去式，主要子句用 would + 原形。

uses.label_zh: 和現在事實相反的想像
uses.form: If + S + V-ed + , + S + would + V（原形）
If + I + were + you + , + I + would + V（原形）
uses.note_zh: 正式寫作用 were，口語也常聽到 was

uses.form: If + S + V-ed + , + S + could / might + V（原形）
uses.signal: could = 有能力／可能；might = 也許

mistakes.wrong: If I would have more money, I would rent a bigger place.
mistakes.right: If I had more money, I would rent a bigger place.
mistakes.why_zh: if 子句用過去式，would 只放在主要子句

mistakes.wrong: If the rent is lower, we would sign today.
mistakes.right: If the rent were lower, we would sign today.
mistakes.why_zh: would 搭配的是第二條件句，if 子句要退一格到過去式

mistakes.wrong: If the landlord fixes the heater, we would stay.
mistakes.right: If the landlord fixes the heater, we'll stay.
mistakes.why_zh: 真的有可能發生就用第一條件句：現在式 + will

examples.en: If the apartment had a balcony, we would take it right away.
examples.zh: 如果那間有陽台，我們馬上就租。（但其實沒有）

examples.en: If I were you, I would ask whether utilities are included.
examples.zh: 如果我是你，我會問清楚有沒有包水電。

examples.en: If we found a roommate, we could afford a bigger place.
examples.zh: 如果我們找到室友，就租得起大一點的地方。

exercises.q: If the apartment ___ (have) a washing machine, we would sign the lease today.
exercises.explain_zh: 和現在事實相反（其實沒有洗衣機），if 子句用過去式 had。

exercises.q: If I ___ (be) you, I would ask for a one-year lease first.
exercises.explain_zh: If I were you 是給建議的固定說法；口語也可以說 was。

exercises.q: If the landlord lowered the rent, we ___ (stay) another year.
exercises.explain_zh: if 子句已經用過去式 lowered，主要子句用 would + 原形。

exercises.q: If the building ___ (allow) pets, my sister would move in tomorrow.
exercises.explain_zh: 主詞 the building 是第三人稱單數，但第二條件句的 if 子句用過去式，所以是 allowed，不是 allows。

exercises.q: We can't afford this place on our own, but if we ___ a roommate, we could.
options: found
will find
would find
have found
exercises.explain_zh: 主要子句是 could（第二條件句），if 子句用過去式 found；if 子句不放 will 或 would。

exercises.q: The landlord says he will fix the heater this week. If he ___ it, we'll stay.
options: fixes
fixed
would fix
had fixed
exercises.explain_zh: 這是很有可能發生的事（他說這週會修），主要子句是 we'll stay，所以用第一條件句：if + 現在式 fixes。

review.point: Making suggestions: Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…
review.point_zh: 提出建議：Why don't we… / I'd suggest that…

exercises.q: Why don't we ___ (ask) the landlord for a two-year lease?
exercises.explain_zh: Why don't we 後面接原形動詞。

exercises.q: I'd suggest that you ___ every room before you move in.
options: photograph
to photograph
photographing
will photograph
exercises.explain_zh: suggest that + 主詞 + 原形動詞（that 子句裡用原形）。

exercises.q: I'd suggest ___ (visit) the apartment at night to check the noise.
exercises.explain_zh: suggest 後面直接接動作時用 V-ing，不接 to V。

guide.key_zh: Why don't we…? 是友善的提議，不是在問為什麼；正式一點用 I'd suggest…

uses.label_zh: 口語、友善的提議：我們要不要…？

uses.note_zh: 美式與正式英文：that 後面用原形，主詞是第三人稱也不加 s（英式常說 should + 原形）

uses.label_zh: 比較正式：建議做某件事

mistakes.wrong: I suggest you to send it.
mistakes.why_zh: suggest 後面不接「人 + to V」

mistakes.wrong: Why we don't ask the team?
mistakes.right: Why don't we ask the team?
mistakes.why_zh: 這是問句，don't 要放在 we 前面

listening.title: Viewing an apartment with the landlord

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Thanks for showing us around. The living room gets a lot more light than I expected.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: It does. The lease is for twelve months, and all utilities are included except internet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: That sounds fair. Can I ask about subletting? My job sometimes sends me abroad for a few months.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: I'd rather you didn't sublet without asking me first. If you told me the person's details in advance, I would probably say yes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: That's reasonable. And how much is the security deposit?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: Two months' rent. You'd get it back within thirty days, as long as there's no damage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Would you mind if we did a walk-through together on move-in day? I'd like to note any marks on the walls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: Not at all. Honestly, if every tenant did that, my life would be much easier.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: One more thing. If I wanted to paint the bedroom, would that be OK?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: Go ahead, as long as you paint it back to white when you leave.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Daniel
lines.text: Great. I still have some vacation days left, so I can take a week off to move in properly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ms. Porter
lines.text: Then why don't we aim for the first of next month?

questions.q: What does Ms. Porter say about subletting?
options: It is never allowed in her building.
She might agree if Daniel tells her about the person beforehand.
Daniel can sublet for up to a few months without asking.
She will charge an extra deposit for it.
questions.explain_zh: 她說「If you told me the person's details in advance, I would probably say yes」，事先告知就可能答應。

questions.q: Why does Daniel want a walk-through on move-in day?
options: To decide which room to paint
To check whether the internet works
To record any marks that are already on the walls
To measure the rooms for furniture
questions.explain_zh: Daniel 說「I'd like to note any marks on the walls」，要先記錄原本就有的痕跡。

questions.q: What can we infer about Ms. Porter?
options: She has never rented out an apartment before.
She has probably had disagreements with tenants about damage.
She plans to raise the rent next year.
She doesn't like tenants who paint the walls.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她說「if every tenant did that, my life would be much easier」，暗示過去常因為損壞責任和房客有爭議。

dictation: If you told me the person's details in advance, I would probably say yes.
Honestly, if every tenant did that, my life would be much easier.
Then why don't we aim for the first of next month?

shadowing: If the rent were a little lower, we would sign today.
It's within walking distance of the station.
Is the security deposit one month or two?
Why don't we do a walk-through together on move-in day?

prompts.question: If you could live anywhere in your city, where would you live? Answer in one or two sentences.
prompts.question_zh: 如果你可以住在你們城市的任何地方，你會住哪裡？用一兩句回答。
hints: If I could live anywhere, I would…
because it's within walking distance of…
prompts.sample: If I could live anywhere, I would live near the river, because it's within walking distance of my office and a big park.

prompts.question: What is one deal-breaker for you when you look at an apartment?
prompts.question_zh: 看房子時，有什麼是你一定不考慮的？
hints: If a place had…, I wouldn't…
prompts.sample: For me, noise is a deal-breaker. If a place had a bar downstairs, I wouldn't even look inside.

writing.task: A friend is looking for an apartment and asks for your advice. Write a short message in three parts: (1) describe your ideal apartment, (2) say what you would do if the rent were too high, and (3) give one suggestion.
writing.task_zh: 朋友在找房子，請你給建議。寫一則短訊息，分三部分：(1) 你理想中的公寓；(2) 如果房租太貴你會怎麼做；(3) 給一個建議。
writing.sample: Hi Jess, good luck with the apartment hunt! My ideal apartment would be bright, quiet and within walking distance of a station. For me, mold is a deal-breaker: I came down with a terrible cough the last time I lived in a damp place. If the rent were too high, I would look for a roommate rather than move into a run-down building. If I were you, I would also ask how much the security deposit is before you visit, so there are no surprises. Why don't you send me the links? I'm happy to look at them with you this weekend.
checklist_zh: 有沒有分成三部分：理想公寓、房租太貴怎麼辦、一個建議
if 子句用過去式（were、had、found），主要子句用 would／could + 原形

translation.zh: 如果這間公寓有陽台，我們今天就會簽約。
translation.en: If this apartment had a balcony, we would sign the lease today.
alt: If this apartment had a balcony, we'd sign the lease today.
If the apartment had a balcony, we would sign the lease today.

translation.zh: 如果我是你，我會先要求看一下水電費帳單。
translation.en: If I were you, I would ask to see the utility bills first.
alt: If I were you, I'd ask to see the utility bills first.

translation.zh: 這一區的房租自去年以來已經上漲了 12%。
translation.en: Rent in this area has gone up by 12% since last year.
alt: Rents in this area have gone up by 12% since last year.
Rent in this area has increased by 12% since last year.
Rent in this area has risen by 12% since last year.

translation.zh: 我們看到那間公寓的時候，已經找房子找了兩個月。
translation.en: When we saw that apartment, we had been looking for a place for two months.
alt: We had been looking for a place for two months when we saw that apartment.
When we saw that apartment, we had been apartment hunting for two months.

translation.zh: 我們搬進去之前，房東已經把廚房重新粉刷好了。
translation.en: Before we moved in, the landlord had already repainted the kitchen.
alt: The landlord had already repainted the kitchen before we moved in.
The landlord had repainted the kitchen before we moved in.

replies.zh: 今天翻譯第 4、5 題放了一組對照：had been looking（到那時為止一直在找，強調持續了多久）vs had already repainted（在那之前就已經完成的一件事），翻譯時留意兩者的差別。

reading.title: The Renewal Letter
paragraphs: When Priya opened the renewal letter from her landlord, her heart sank. After three years in the apartment, her rent was going up by fifteen percent, a figure that seemed to have been plucked out of thin air. Her first instinct was to fire off an angry email. Instead, she slept on it.

The next morning she did her homework. Asking rents for similar one-bedrooms on her street had risen by around six percent, not fifteen. She also knew something the letter didn't mention: her landlord, Mr. Haddad, had struggled to fill the apartment upstairs, which had sat empty for most of the summer. Every month a unit stays vacant, an owner loses income but still has to cover the mortgage, so a reliable tenant who pays on time is worth more than the asking price suggests.

Priya decided to make her case in writing, keeping the tone friendly but firm. She pointed out that she had never missed a payment, had reported problems promptly, and had even paid out of pocket to fix a leaky faucet. She attached three comparable listings and proposed an eight percent increase in exchange for signing a two-year lease. She ended by saying she hoped to stay, but that if the increase went ahead as planned, she would have no choice but to start looking elsewhere.

Mr. Haddad called two days later. He wouldn't go as low as eight, he said, but he could live with ten, provided she signed for two years. Priya had been prepared to accept twelve, so she agreed on the spot. Her friends were amazed that she hadn't simply paid up. "Most landlords would rather keep a good tenant than gamble on a stranger," she told them. "You just have to give them a reason to say yes."

questions.q: Why was the empty apartment upstairs important to Priya's strategy?
options: It meant she could move upstairs if the talks failed.
It suggested Mr. Haddad could not afford to lose another tenant.
It proved that rents on her street were falling.
It showed that Mr. Haddad was planning to sell the building.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第二段說空房期間房東沒有收入卻還得付房貸，所以準時付租的好房客很有價值，這就是 Priya 的談判籌碼。

questions.q: What did Priya offer in exchange for a smaller increase?
options: To pay for future repairs herself
To pay several months' rent in advance
To sign a two-year lease
To find a tenant for the apartment upstairs
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：她提議漲 8%，條件是簽兩年租約（in exchange for signing a two-year lease）。

questions.q: What can we infer from the fact that Priya "had been prepared to accept twelve"?
options: She got a better deal than she expected.
She regretted agreeing too quickly.
Mr. Haddad had originally offered twelve percent.
Her friends had advised her to accept twelve percent.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她本來願意接受 12%，結果只漲 10%，所以結果比她預期的好，才會當場答應。

questions.q: In paragraph 1, a figure "plucked out of thin air" is one that
options: was copied from another landlord's letter
was chosen without any clear reason behind it
was calculated very carefully
was hidden in the small print
questions.explain_zh: out of thin air 表示憑空冒出來；第二段也說附近行情只漲約 6%，可見 15% 沒有根據。

listening.title: So you haggled with your landlord?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: So, wait, you actually haggled with your landlord? Like, in writing?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Well, sort of. I sent him a letter with three listings attached, and—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Hang on, three listings? You went full lawyer on him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Hardly. I just wanted to show I wasn't pulling numbers out of thin air the way he was.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Fair enough. But weren't you worried he'd just say, "Fine, move out"?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Honestly? A little. But the apartment upstairs sat empty all summer. If he lost me too, he'd be bleeding money.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: Huh. I'd never have thought of that. I'd probably just pay up and grumble about it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: That's what most people do, which is kind of why landlords keep trying it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: So what did he come back with?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Ten percent, as long as I sign for two years. I was ready to go to twelve, so—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Tom
lines.text: So you basically won. Okay, if I ever get one of those letters, you're writing my reply.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Priya
lines.text: Deal. But you're buying the coffee.

questions.q: Why wasn't Priya very worried about being told to move out?
options: She had already found another apartment.
Her lease protected her from rent increases.
Losing her would cost the landlord money, since the upstairs apartment was empty.
Tom had offered her a room.
questions.explain_zh: 她說樓上空了一整個夏天，「If he lost me too, he'd be bleeding money」，房東承擔不起再失去一個房客。

questions.q: What does Tom mean by "You went full lawyer on him"?
options: Priya threatened to take the landlord to court.
Priya was surprisingly formal and well prepared.
Priya hired a lawyer to write the letter.
Priya was rude to the landlord.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：Tom 聽到她附了三份行情資料，開玩笑說她像律師一樣準備周全，不是真的找律師或告人。

questions.q: What does Tom say he would probably do in Priya's situation?
options: Pay the higher rent and complain about it
Ask Priya to negotiate for him right away
Move out immediately
Ask for a shorter lease
questions.explain_zh: Tom 說「I'd probably just pay up and grumble about it」：乖乖付錢，然後抱怨。

dictation: But the apartment upstairs sat empty all summer.
If he lost me too, he'd be bleeding money.
Ten percent, as long as I sign for two years.

glossary.definition: from nowhere, without any clear reason or source
waited until the next day before making a decision
losing a lot of money continuously
